result: Findings written to `/tmp/findings/flags.md`. ## Summary **`p_flags` (info_phdrN "Flags:")** — pure function of `p_flags & 7`; concatenate in order, no separator: - `R` if bit 0x4, `W` if bit 0x2, `X` if bit 0x1 - Table: 0→`` (empty), 1→`X`, 2→`W`, 3→`WX`, 4→`R`, 5→`RX`, 6→`RW`, 7→`RWX` - **All other bits are silently ignored** — every single bit `1<<3 .. 1<<31` renders empty; `0xf0000000`→``, `0x0ff00000`→``, `0xff`→`RWX`, `0xffffffff`→`RWX` - Empty result = literally `` (no `0`, no ` `) **`sh_flags` (info_shdrN "Flags:")** — pure function of `sh_flags & 7`; concatenate in order, no separator: - `W` if bit 0x1, `A` if bit 0x2, `X` if bit 0x4 - Table: 0→`0`, 1→`W`, 2→`A`, 3→`WA`, 4→`X`, 5→`WX`, 6→`AX`, 7→`WAX` - **All other bits ignored** — MERGE/STRINGS/INFO_LINK/LINK_ORDER/GROUP/TLS/COMPRESSED/MASKOS/MASKPROC and bit 0x8 produce nothing. `0x8`→`0`, `0x10`→`0`, `0x400`→`0`, every `1<<3..1<<63`→`0`, `0xfff`→`WAX`, `0xffffffffffffffff`→`WAX` - Empty result = literal single char `0` (not the numeric value — `0x10` prints `0`, not `16`/`0x10`) - **32-bit vs 64-bit: identical rendering.** Field is read as u64 on 64-bit (proven via big-endian: `endian=2,bits=64,sh_flags=1`→`W`, which a 4-byte read would have shown as `0`), u32 on 32-bit; only bits 0..2 are consulted either way. **Coverage (0 mismatches against the rules):** p_flags = 0..255, each `1<<0..1<<31`, `0xff00`, `0xffff0000`, `0xfffffff8`, `0x0ff00000`, `0xf0000000`, `0xffffffff` — × {64,32}bit × {LE,BE}. sh_flags = all 0x000..0xfff, each `1<<0..1<<63` (64-bit) / `1<<0..1<<31` (32-bit), all-ones — × {64,32}bit × {LE,BE}. **Independence:** rendering does not depend on `p_type` / `sh_type` (the Flags row is always present, even for PT_NULL / SHT_NULL), nor on `e_machine`, `e_type`, `osabi`. The `info_segmentN` / `info_sectionN` tables have no Flags row at all. **Bonus — a third "Flags:" row exists**, easily confused: `fileinfo_e_flags` renders `format!("{:#x}", e_flags)` (lowercase, `0x` prefix, unpadded, no `` wrapper), sits **last** in the fileinfo table after `fileinfo_sh`, and the **entire `` is omitted when `e_flags == 0`**. **Key asymmetry to not get wrong:** `W` and `X` appear in both letter sets but at different bit positions — `W`=0x2/`X`=0x1 for p_flags vs `W`=0x1/`X`=0x4 for sh_flags; and the empty-case fallback differs (`` vs `0`). Byte-span classes: 64-bit `p_flags 0x44..0x48`, `sh_flags 0x80..0x88`; 32-bit `p_flags 0x4c..0x50`, `sh_flags 0x5c..0x60` (standard ELF offsets).

Findings written to **/tmp/findings/bitness.md** Key results: **1. ELF32 layout is correct.** ehdr spans: `ident 0..0x10` (identical to ELF64), `e_type 0x10..0x12`, `e_machine 0x12..0x14`, `e_version 0x14..0x18`, then 4-byte `e_entry 0x18..0x1c`, `e_phoff 0x1c..0x20`, `e_shoff 0x20..0x24`, `e_flags 0x24..0x28`, then six 2-byte fields `0x28..0x34`. phdr entry = 32 B with the correct ELF32 order `p_type,p_offset,p_vaddr,p_paddr,p_filesz,p_memsz,p_flags,p_align` (flags at entry+24). shdr entry = 40 B, `sh_flags` 4 B at entry+8. Cross-validated against a real `gcc -m32 -c` object vs `readelf -S` — all 14 shdr spans at 40-byte stride and all section content ranges matched. **2. Big-endian decoding is correct.** A properly BE-encoded file yields identical fileinfo values to its LE twin. Decisive negative test: LE bytes with `EI_DATA=2` produce `Type: Unknown 512`, `Architecture: Unknown: 15872`, `Entrypoint: 0x10000000000000`, `e_phentsize 14336`, `e_shentsize 16384`, `ehdr` span `0..0x4000` — every integer byte-swapped, including `e_ehsize` and `sh_name`. **3. `e_phentsize`/`e_shentsize` are completely ignored.** Strides and span sizes are hardcoded per class: phdr 32/56, shdr 40/64. Proven three ways: phentsize=0/40/64 all give 56-byte spans on ELF64; a table physically laid out at 64-byte stride with `phentsize=64` is misparsed (`info_phdr1` reads garbage `Type: Unknown: 4008636142`); and the EOF bound panics at `phoff+56` / `shoff+40` etc. regardless of the header value (`src/elf/elfxx.rs:174:46` for phdr, `:227:46` for shdr, message `range end index N out of range for slice of length M`). **4. `ehdr` span is `0..e_ehsize`, confirmed.** Panics at `src/elf/parser.rs:117:18` iff `e_ehsize == 0` (index `18446744073709551615`, usize underflow) or `e_ehsize > file_size` (index `e_ehsize-1`). All 22 header field spans are still emitted at their fixed offsets when `e_ehsize` is small (raw HTML for ehsize=1/20/33 included, with `starts_at`/`ends_at` maps proving the start-at-`start`/end-count-at-`end-1`/blind-pop model). Minimum file size gate is the hardcoded 52/64, *not* `e_ehsize`. **5.** All 10 fileinfo rows have identical `` names, labels and order for both classes; only `fileinfo_class` differs (`32-bit`/`64-bit`). Optional 11th row `fileinfo_e_flags` (`Flags: 0x...`, plain hex, no span) appears only when `e_flags != 0`, identical in both classes. `highlightClasses()` (16 entries) and `connect()` lists are byte-identical across class and endianness. **6. End-to-end LE vs BE on real byte-swapped ELF32 and ELF64 objects:** span ranges, all info tables (including `.shstrtab`-resolved section names), connects, highlights, `#offsets`, `fileLen` and line counts all identical. The only diffs are the `fileinfo_data` row text and the hex/ascii bytes themselves.

Newline is a *terminator* after byte `i` where `i%16==15`, so a trailing `\n` sits before `` iff `n%16==0`; a partial last line has none. `\n` count = `floor(n/16)`. **#offsets** — lowercase hex, **no `0x` prefix, no zero padding, no fixed width** (`…f0\n100\n110…`, `…ff0\n1000…`, `…fff0\n10000…`). `ceil(n/16)` entries, `floor(n/16)` newlines — same trailing-newline rule as #ascii. Findings written to **/tmp/findings/order.md**

## Global insertion order (6 phases, fully pinned)

1. `ehdr` = `[0, e_ehsize)`
2. the 13 non-ident ehdr fields: `e_type … e_shstrndx`
3. `for i in 0..e_phnum`: `bin_segment{i}` (if not skipped) → `bin_phdr{i}` → its 8 `p_*` fields — **per-index interleaved**, segment before its own phdr
4. `for i in 0..e_shnum`: `bin_section{i}` (if not skipped) → `bin_shdr{i}` → its 10 `sh_*` fields — **per-index interleaved**, section before its own shdr
5. `ident`, `magic`, `class`, `data`, `ver`, `abi`, `abi_ver`, `pad` — **the e_ident group is pushed AFTER all phdr/shdr/segment/section ranges** (surprising; proven with `phoff=0`/`shoff=0`)
6. `segment_subrange` note pass — **last**, after the ident group, in (segment index, note order)

Pinning probe: 64-bit `phoff=0,phnum=1,shoff=0,shnum=1` gives
`['ehdr','bin_phdr0 phdr','p_type','bin_shdr0 shdr','sh_name','ident','magic']`.

## Skips (silent, `#bytes` only — info tables + connect() are still emitted)
- segment: `p_filesz == 0` **OR `p_offset == 0`** (new: offset-0 skip; `p_type` irrelevant)
- section: `sh_size == 0` **OR `sh_type == 8` (NOBITS) OR `sh_offset == 0`**; sweep 0..24 shows only type 8 skipped — `SHT_NULL` is emitted
- phdr/shdr/ehdr ranges: never skipped

## Panics (exit 101, no HTML)
- range add: `start >= L` → `parser.rs:116:18`, `index = start`; else `end-1 >= L` → `parser.rs:117:18`, `index = end-1` (`end==0` → `18446744073709551615`). `end == L` is fine.
- phdr table parse → `elfxx.rs:174:46`; shdr table → `elfxx.rs:227:46`, messages `range start index S out of range for slice of length L` (if `S > L`) else `range end index E …`; fails on first non-fitting entry.
- note loop reads → `parser.rs:351/352/353:39`, `range end index 4|8|12 out of range for slice of length {remaining}` for remaining 1-3 / 4-7 / 8-11.
- Check order: ehdr range → phdr parse → segment/phdr ranges → shdr parse → section/shdr ranges → note pass (each proven by dueling-panic tests).

## Other
- **`e_phentsize`/`e_shentsize` are completely ignored** — stride and box length are hardcoded 56/64 (64-bit), 32/40 (32-bit).
- `phoff==0`/`shoff==0` with count>0: parsed normally at offset 0, ranges overlap the ehdr.
- `ehdr` range = `[0, e_ehsize)` raw, unclamped; ehdr field ranges always at fixed offsets.
- note subrange length = `12 + align4(namesz) + align4(descsz)`; `total > remaining` → silent break.
- Output is deterministic; no dedup of identical ranges.
